ground_truth.title: Perfect Your Pour—Here Are the 5 Best Gooseneck Kettles for Coffee Lovers
ground_truth.author: Jesse Porter
ground_truth.main_content:
Maximize the flavor of your coffee or tea with precision

You've seen them at your favorite local coffee shop, and you've appreciated their classic design and tapered elegance, but rest assured that gooseneck kettles aren't all about aesthetics. The signature pouring spout that gives the kettle its name is an integral component to specialized methods of coffee and preparation, as it dispenses a consistent and precise flow of hot water, allowing for deliberate and controlled saturation of tea leaves or ground beans.

And with the advent of precise temperature control in the gooseneck kettle realm, it's now possible to lend even more specificity to the painstaking creation of hot beverages, resulting in ever greater flavor extraction. We tested many gooseneck kettles, paying attention to capacity, heating time, and precision when pouring. These are our favorites.

Best Overall

Fellow Stagg EKG Pro Electric Gooseneck Kettle

What We Like

- Program temperature by single degrees
- Temperature hold function
- Precision pour
- Stylish

What We Don't Like

- Expensive
- Small capacity

Blending style and technology in a svelte and attractive package, the Fellow Stagg EKG Pour-Over Kettle boasts convenient features and great design. It's impossible to ignore the Stagg's smooth slopes, sharp edges, and gorgeous gooseneck spout, not to mention its austere matte colorway that differentiates it from the plethora of stainless steel goosenecks on the market. (It's also available in a polished copper finish.)

The technological bells and whistles, though, set the Stagg EKG apart from the pack, as its list of features established it as one of the most modern and advanced kettles we tested. It has a manual temperature input with LCD screen, which allows the user to select any water temperature between 135 and 212 degrees Fahrenheit. There's also the option to maintain water temperature for up to one hour, as well as a built-in stopwatch for timing pour-over coffee or tea. It's even Bluetooth compatible, making it one of the few kettles you can operate right from your phone.

If the Stagg EKG is the sports car of the gooseneck kettle realm, it has a sticker price to match, clocking in at a cost that's well above many of the other kettles on this list. That cost gets you performance, as this unit only took five minutes to reach a boil in our tests, among the fastest we came across, and features a spout that pours consistently and precisely. For the serious fan of or loose-leaf teas, the Stagg EKG is among the best kettle options.

Capacity: 30 ounces | Dimensions: 11.1 x 6.7 x 7.7 inches | Temperature Range: 104–212 degrees Fahrenheit

Easiest to Use

Cosori Electric Gooseneck Kettle

What We Like

- Five temperature presets
- Sleek design
- Reasonably priced
- Easy to use

What We Don't Like

- Exterior gets hot
- Small capacity

Despite not boasting every one of the high-tech features found in the Fellow Stagg EKG, the aesthetically reminiscent Cosori Electric Gooseneck Kettle is nonetheless extremely serviceable for all hot beverage needs. Featuring straightforward push-button orientation, the Cosori offers five different temperature settings designated for specific beverages: 170 degrees Fahrenheit for white tea while green tea gets 180 degrees, the coffee setting is 205 degrees, and of course, there's a 212 degrees button for boiling water.

The attractive gooseneck design of the Cosori features a minimalist matte black finish and a comfortable handle. The electric kettle does get quite hot when in use, so users should be sure to always pick it up from the handle only. But the heating is relatively quick, and the temperature was maintained for 30 minutes or more in our tests.

With a capacity of only 27 ounces, the Cosori was one of the smaller kettles in our tests, so it might not be ideal for beverage aficionados who need more than three or four cups at a time. Other than its size, however, the Cosori scored high in every respect, and we found that it offers great aesthetics and solid performance at a reasonable price.

Capacity: 27 ounces | Dimensions: 11.6 x 9 x 7.7 inches | Temperature Range: 170–212 degrees Fahrenheit

Best Budget

Coffee Gator Gooseneck Kettle

What We Like

- Durable
- Works on all stovetops
- Precise, reliable spout
- Built-in thermometer

What We Don't Like

- Prone to rust
- A little loud

Stovetop kettles require a bit more attention from the user, as the heat source is independent from the kettle, and must be manually turned off once the desired temperature is reached. While this can potentially lead to a lot of guesswork, the Coffee Gator Gooseneck Kettle eliminates this variable with its clever inclusion of a thermometer built into the lid handle. This onboard manual thermometer measures the water temperature and displays it clearly, so the attentive user can remove the kettle from the heat source at just the right time.

In addition to the handy integrated thermometer, the Coffee Gator kettle also boasts a handsome design, an ergonomic handle, and a gooseneck spout that delivers a reliably controlled pour. Between the temperature gauge and the consistent pour, there's no loss of precision with this stovetop model. The unit also works on all types of ranges, even induction burners.

The only downside we observed with the Coffee Gator was that it emits a slight whirring sound when it's heating up, but that's a small price to pay for this type of quality. Speaking of price, that might be the Coffee Gator's top selling point—it was among the most reasonably priced kettles we tested.

Capacities: 34 ounces, 40 ounces | Dimensions: 10.15 x 5.6 x 5.2 inches, 10.2 x 6.2 x 5.4 inches

Best Compact

Lardera Smart Electric Kettle

What We Like

- Compact and lightweight
- Precise, no-drip pouring
- Durable materials

What We Don't Like

- Temperature adjustment hard to use

With coffee makers shrinking so much in recent years that some models now fit comfortably into indiscreet drawers in hotel rooms, it's no surprise that there are size-conscious units in the realm of gooseneck kettles as well. The Lardera Smart Electric Kettle scored high marks in our tests, yet it will take up much less space on your countertop than models that scored similarly or worse.

Measuring only 10 inches from spout to handle, and with a base that's only six inches across, the electric Lardera unit was one of the smaller models we tested. Despite that, it offers solid construction, slick aesthetics, and a smooth pour. It was also one of the more efficient models we examined, with the water reaching a boil in just three and a half minutes when the kettle is full.

Our only gripe regarding the Lardera was that its touch-sensitive temperature adjustment was somewhat tricky to use—we found that it may take a few attempts of sliding your finger to land on the exact temperature you want. Other than that, the Lardera delivers sturdy construction and consistent heating in a package that can only be described as small but mighty.

Capacity: 30 ounces | Dimensions: 6.5 x 4.5 x 10 inches | Temperature Range: 170–212 degrees Fahrenheit

Fastest Heat-Up Time

Bodum Melior Electric Gooseneck Kettle

What We Like

- Fast heating
- Low-priced
- Easy to use

What We Don't Like

- No temperature gauge
- Smaller capacity

A kitchenware manufacturer founded in Denmark in 1944, Bodum will be a familiar brand name to any fans of French press coffee, as the firm has been marketing several popular French press models for decades now. What better way to elevate your French press game than with an electric kettle from the same trusted brand?

The Bodum Melior Electric Gooseneck Kettle earned top marks in our tests for its heating speed, serving up piping hot water in around three minutes. As French press and other immersion methods require a few extra minutes for brewing, it's an attractive proposition to cut down water heating time, and the Bodum Melior rises to the occasion in that department.

We were big fans of its handsome matte black finish and its distinctive handle and lid, which are finished in sustainable and heat-resistant natural cork. With a capacity of only 27 ounces, it's on the economical side in terms of total volume, but it's fortunately also on the economical end of the price spectrum as well.

Capacity: 27 ounces | Dimensions: 11.8 x 6.3 x 8.3 inches | Temperature Range: 170–212 degrees Fahrenheit

Final Verdict

Boasting high-end features like temperature control, Bluetooth connectivity, and more, the Fellow Stagg EKG Kettle is the most impressive gooseneck kettle to come out of our tests. Also scoring high marks at a fraction of the price is the Cosori Electric Gooseneck Kettle. It offers a similarly sleek design and some nice features of its own in a more economical package.

How We Tested Gooseneck Kettles

Our testing lab examined top-rated gooseneck kettles side-by-side in 2022, and we've continued to test models in our home kitchens since then. For each gooseneck kettle, we analyzed important attributes including the time it takes to heat the water and how accurate the final temperature is. Additionally, we note the capacity, comfort, and any other important features.

Other Options We Tested

The Bean Envy Gooseneck Pour-Over Kettle was well-reviewed in our tests, with its larger 40-ounce capacity earning special notice. We also appreciated its integrated thermometer, although the temperature readouts around 200 degrees became a little imprecise. We also felt that the handle on this unit felt a little cheap, but this wasn't a major detraction, especially given the reasonable price.

The BonJour Gooseneck Kettle offers a relatively massive capacity of 64 ounces, making it an ideal choice for any coffee or tea applications in which total volume is a primary consideration. It's a sturdy and reliable stovetop option that offers fantastic performance — albeit with less precision in the pouring department, due to its wider spout.

What to Look for in a Gooseneck Kettle

Electric vs. Stovetop

The heat source—internal versus external—is the primary consideration when choosing a gooseneck kettle. Electric models plug into a socket and utilize an onboard heating element, making them versatile for spaces that might not have a stove available, such as an office or a dorm room. Stovetop models, meanwhile, require a stove or other external heat source, but they score extra points for portability and simplicity, with no cords or bulky base to consider. Both categories offer models that come with temperature control, although precision is generally higher with electric units. That said, price tends to be better in the stovetop category.

Capacity

Gooseneck kettles come in a range of sizes, with most adequately sized to heat enough water for a few cups of coffee or tea. Certain gooseneck kettles are more capacious, making them good candidates for filling up extra-large mugs, or for serving up enough hot water to meet the beverage needs of any party or gathering.

Cleaning

Since most gooseneck kettles utilize stainless steel in their construction (on the interior, the exterior, or both), the user needs to do what they can to prevent rust, and to protect the finish. After use, it's advised to fully dry your gooseneck kettle, and to wash it with soap and water at regular intervals. From time to time, a solution of water and white vinegar can be used to deep-clean the kettle to prevent the buildup of "scale" from limestone in the water. Finally, for stovetop models being used on a gas range, make sure that the flame isn't wide enough to lick up around the sides of the kettle, which can lead to discoloration.

FAQs

Why would you need a gooseneck kettle?

When dealing with loose-leaf teas or non-electric coffee preparation methods like pour-over, French press, or drip cone, a gooseneck kettle can be an invaluable tool for ensuring a smooth and controlled flow of appropriately-heated water. Kettles with spouts that are larger and more imprecise may do a fine job of dispensing hot water quickly, but certain methods of coffee and tea preparation are all about precision.

What is coffee blooming?

"Blooming" is a term that refers to the off-gassing of carbon dioxide that occurs when freshly-ground coffee beans are initially saturated with water. Whether you're making pour-over coffee, or using an immersion process like French press, allowing your coffee beans to bloom is an essential step on the journey to pristine flavor.

"The bloom process is imperative, and there is some science to it," says Nigel Price, the founder and owner of Drip Coffee Makers in New York City. "Gasses come out of coffee when it's freshly ground. If the coffee isn't allowed to breathe and let those gasses out, you don't allow the coffee beans to get to their fullest potential of saturation during the steeping process."

Do gooseneck kettles whistle?

Gooseneck kettles generally do not whistle, so if you're using a stovetop model, you'll want to keep an eye on it to make sure it doesn't boil over and/or overflow. If it's an electric model, however, it will likely have an automatic shut-off feature. It may also have a thermometer on the lid so users can see when the water has reached the preferred temperature.
